validity.recommendation: no action on existence, classification, or duplicate status -- well documented and correctly distinguished from P0207 Kern River Gas Pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION strongly confirmed by 7+ independent primary/regulatory sources spanning 1990-2024, none of which is GEM/gem.wiki: PHMSA Notice of Proposed Safety Order CPF No. 5-2012-1008S (2012, direct fetch); PHMSA Failure Investigation Report -- El Paso-Mojave GT 2012-5-2 (2013, retrieved via Wayback after the live phmsa.dot.gov URL 403'd -- blocked, not deleted, so the original harvested citation is kept and the Wayback capture added alongside per the no-delete-on-block rule); CPUC Decision 90-10-034 (Oct 12, 1990, California PUC, wholly independent of any pipeline-company or federal-regulator chain); USGS Open-File Report 92-447 (1992, a federal geological survey of Mojave Desert pipeline corridors, wholly independent of PHMSA/SEC/company sources -- confirms route, ~142-mile Topock-Daggett segment, and 1991 construction); El Paso Natural Gas Co.'s own FY1993 SEC 10-K (filed 1994, the ORIGINAL owner's own contemporaneous account of the just-completed system); Kinder Morgan's FY2013 and FY2023 10-Ks/Exhibit 21.1 (current corporate parent, two different filing years); Kinder Morgan's current Operations/Natural-Gas/Index corporate page; and Oil & Gas Journal's 1993 trade-press coverage. CLASSIFICATION as an interstate FERC-jurisdictional natural gas transmission pipeline is correct (PHMSA docs, SEC filings, and CPUC decision all agree). NOT A DUPLICATE of P0207 Kern River Gas Pipeline: the two systems share a jointly-held 'Common Facilities' segment between Daggett, CA and the Bifurcation Point near Arvin, CA (undivided interest -- 25% Mojave Pipeline Company LLC / 75% Kern River Gas Transmission Company, per KMI's FY2013 10-K, and independently corroborated by USGS OFR 92-447's ~83-mile shared-conduit description), but Mojave's own exclusive mainline runs Topock, AZ -> Daggett, CA while Kern River's own exclusive mainline runs Opal, WY -> Daggett, CA -- distinct origins, distinct current ultimate ownership (Mojave = Kinder Morgan/El Paso lineage; Kern River = Berkshire Hathaway Energy, per P0207's own shard), and the shared-facilities relationship is a known, expected, non-duplicative structure (also flagged the other direction in P0207's cross_row_leads, whose USGS-sourced lead is consistent with and corroborated by this research).

validity.researcher_notes: Three independent sources converge on 1992 as the in-service/commissioning year, none supporting the sheet's current StartYear1 = 1991: El Paso Natural Gas Co.'s own FY1993 10-K (filed 1994) states MPC's 'pipeline facilities ... commenced operations on March 1, 1992' (also: 'FERC issued orders [in 1990] authorizing MPC to construct and operate its pipeline facilities' -- construction followed that 1990 authorization); PHMSA's 2012 NOPSO states 'The Mojave Pipeline was built between 1991-1992'; PHMSA's 2013 Failure Investigation Report states 'The Mojave Pipeline was built and commissioned in 1992.' This is the same StartYear1 1991->1992 correction pattern P0207 (Kern River, this same batch) independently found for its own sibling system, entering service Feb. 15, 1992 -- both California-import pipelines commissioned within weeks of each other in early 1992, which is an internally consistent, mutually-corroborating pair, not a coincidence to be suspicious of.

validity.researcher_notes: 804.70 km converts to almost exactly 500 mi (500 x 1.609344 = 804.67 km), and 'approximately 500 miles' / '500-mile' is stated explicitly and independently by: PHMSA's 2012 NOPSO ('MPOC ... operates approximately 500 miles of pipeline') and Kinder Morgan's current Operations/Natural-Gas/Index page ('The Mojave Pipeline is a 500-mile pipeline system'). CAVEAT -- two other primary sources give different figures for different eras/scopes, read together as a plausible growth history rather than an error: El Paso Natural Gas Co.'s own FY1993 10-K (filed 1994, at commissioning) states 'MPC's system consists of approximately 400 miles of pipeline with one mainline compressor station' -- the ORIGINAL, just-completed system; that same 1993 filing separately describes a then-proposed (never observed as built in any later source) 475 MMcf/d, ~352-mile northward extension toward Sacramento/East Bay that ran into a FERC/CPUC jurisdictional dispute (also the subject of the OGJ 1993 article) -- no later source shows this extension exists, consistent with GEM's system remaining ~500 mi rather than ~850+ mi. Separately, Kinder Morgan's FY2013 10-K states an unrepeated 'approximate 562-mile Mojave Pipeline system' figure -- a single one-off occurrence, not corroborated in KMI's own FY2016 or FY2023 filings or any other source reviewed, possibly reflecting a different mile-counting convention (e.g., cumulative lateral/loop footage). Retaining the sheet's 804.70 km given two clean, current, independent matches.

Retaining 400.00 MMcf/d given the pipeline's own contemporaneous filing plus independent trade-press corroboration.
